senses.def: a mark, sign, or small amount that shows someone or something was present
examples: The hikers vanished without a trace.
Tests found traces of the drug in his blood.

senses.def: to find someone or something by carefully following signs or information
examples: Police traced the stolen car to a garage in New Jersey.
The call was traced to a phone booth downtown.

senses.def: to find the origin or development of something
examples: She can trace her family back to the 1600s.
The outbreak was traced to contaminated lettuce.

note: Also: to copy a drawing by following its lines through thin paper.

senses.def: the metal rails a train runs on
examples: The train to Boston leaves from track 9.
Never walk on the railroad tracks.

senses.def: marks left by a person, animal, or vehicle, a rough path, or a course for racing
examples: We followed the deer tracks through the snow.
She runs four laps around the track every morning.

senses.def: one song or piece of music on an album
examples: The third track on the album is my favorite.

senses.def: to follow or find someone or something, or to record their progress over time
examples: The app tracks your sleep and heart rate.
Police tracked the suspect to a motel.

note: "Keep track of" = stay informed about; "lose track of time" = not notice time passing. "Track record" = past performance.

senses.def: the activity of buying, selling, or exchanging goods and services, especially between countries
examples: Trade between the two countries has doubled in five years.
The new agreement removes barriers to free trade.

senses.def: a job that needs special skill with your hands
examples: He learned the plumbing trade from his father.

senses.tr: ticaret yapmak, alıp satmak; takas etmek
senses.def: to buy and sell goods, or to exchange one thing for another
examples: The company trades with partners in over thirty countries.
I'll trade you my sandwich for your chips.

note: "Trade-off" = a balance between two things you can't have together. "Trade in" an old car = give it as part payment.

senses.def: a name, symbol, or design that only one company is legally allowed to use for its products
examples: The company sued a rival for using its trademark without permission.
The logo was registered as a trademark in 1998.

senses.def: a typical feature or way of behaving that people connect with a particular person
examples: Bright red glasses became the designer's trademark.

note: Often used like an adjective: "his trademark grin" = his typical, well-known grin.

senses.def: the activity of buying and selling goods, shares, or other things
examples: Trading on Wall Street was suspended after the sharp drop.
Online trading has made investing easier for ordinary people.

note: "Insider trading" = illegally buying or selling shares using secret company information.

senses.def: a belief, custom, or way of doing something that has existed for a long time in a group
examples: It's a family tradition to eat turkey on Thanksgiving.
The town has a long tradition of hosting a summer music festival.

senses.def: following beliefs, customs, or ways of doing things that have existed for a long time
examples: The restaurant serves traditional Turkish dishes.
They had a traditional church wedding.

senses.def: of a type that has been used for a long time, rather than new or modern
examples: Online courses are now as popular as traditional classroom teaching.

senses.def: the vehicles moving on a road at a particular time
examples: I was stuck in traffic for an hour this morning.
Traffic is always heavy on Friday afternoons.

senses.def: the movement of planes, ships, people, or data along a route
examples: The new post brought a lot of traffic to our website.

senses.def: illegal trade in something, such as drugs or weapons
examples: The task force aims to stop the traffic in illegal weapons.

note: Uncountable: "a lot of traffic", not "many traffics". "Human trafficking" = insan kaçakçılığı.

senses.def: a very sad event or situation, especially one that involves death
examples: The town is still recovering from the tragedy of last year's flood.
It's a tragedy that so much food goes to waste.

senses.def: a serious play or story with a sad ending
examples: "Romeo and Juliet" is one of Shakespeare's best-known tragedies.

note: Opposite (in drama): comedy.

senses.def: very sad, usually because someone has died or suffered a lot
examples: She died in a tragic car accident at the age of 24.
The fire was a tragic loss for the whole community.

senses.def: connected with tragedy as a type of play or story
examples: Hamlet is the classic tragic hero.

senses.def: a line of marks or signs left by someone or something
examples: The wounded animal left a trail of blood in the snow.
Investigators followed a paper trail of bank transfers.

senses.def: a path through the countryside, especially for walking
examples: We hiked the trail up to the waterfall.

senses.def: to pull something behind you, or to be pulled along behind
examples: Her long dress trailed on the floor behind her.

senses.def: to be behind others in a race, competition, or election
examples: The home team trailed by six points at halftime.

note: "Blaze a trail" = be the first to do something new (öncülük etmek).

senses.def: a vehicle without an engine pulled by a car or truck
examples: He hitched the boat trailer to his pickup truck.

senses.def: (American) a large vehicle that people can live in, pulled by a car or parked in one place
examples: They lived in a trailer while they built their new house.

senses.def: a short series of scenes from a movie, shown to advertise it
examples: The new trailer for the movie got ten million views in a day.

note: American "trailer" (mobile home) = British "caravan". "Fragman" = trailer.

senses.def: a line of connected railroad cars pulled by an engine
examples: I take the train to work every day.
The last train to Philadelphia leaves at 11:40.

senses.def: to teach a person or animal the skills for a job or activity, or to be taught
examples: All staff are trained in first aid.
She trained as a nurse before going to medical school.

senses.def: to prepare for a sports event by exercising and practicing
examples: He's training for his first marathon.

note: "Train of thought" = a connected series of thoughts: "Sorry, I lost my train of thought."

senses.def: a person who teaches skills to people or animals, especially in sport or fitness
examples: She hired a personal trainer to help her get in shape.
The horse's trainer has won the race three times.

senses.def: (British) a shoe for sports or casual wear
examples: He wore jeans and a pair of white trainers.

note: For the shoe, Americans say "sneakers" or "tennis shoes"; "trainers" is British.

senses.def: the process of learning or teaching the skills needed for a job
examples: New employees receive two weeks of training.
The program offers job training for young people.

senses.def: physical exercise and practice to prepare for a sports event
examples: She's in training for the Olympics.

note: Uncountable: "some training", not "a training". For one event, say "a training session".

senses.def: a particular quality, especially in someone's personality
examples: Patience is his best trait.
Some personality traits are partly inherited from our parents.

note: In American English the final t is pronounced: /treɪt/.

senses.def: a single act of buying, selling, or moving money
examples: The bank charges a fee for each international transaction.
All transactions are recorded and checked for fraud.

senses.def: a written or printed copy of words that were spoken
examples: The court released a full transcript of the trial.
Read the transcript of the podcast if you can't listen to it.

senses.def: (American) an official record of a student's courses and grades
examples: Applicants must send their high school transcripts to the admissions office.

senses.def: to move someone or something from one place, group, or account to another
examples: I'll transfer the money to your account tonight.
The patient was transferred to a larger hospital.

senses.def: to move to a different job, school, or team
examples: She transferred to a university closer to home after her first year.

senses.def: the act of moving someone or something from one place to another
examples: The bank transfer took three days to go through.
The player asked for a transfer to another club.

note: Verb stress is often on the second syllable (trans-FER); noun stress on the first (TRANS-fer). Spelling: transferred, transferring.

senses.def: to change the form, appearance, or character of something completely, usually for the better
examples: Smartphones have transformed the way we communicate.
They transformed the old warehouse into luxury apartments.

note: "Transform" suggests a big, complete change; "change" can be small.

senses.def: a complete change in someone or something
examples: The city has undergone a dramatic transformation over the past decade.
Her transformation from shy student to confident leader surprised everyone.

senses.def: the process of moving people or goods from one place to another
examples: Some of the packages were damaged in transit.
Passengers in transit do not need a visa.

senses.def: (American) a system of buses, trains, etc. for the public
examples: The city is investing billions in public transit.

note: American "public transit" = British "public transport".

senses.def: the process or period of changing from one state or condition to another
examples: The transition from high school to college can be difficult.
The country is in transition to democracy.

note: Also a verb: "The company is transitioning to electric vehicles."

senses.def: to change spoken or written words into another language
examples: Can you translate this letter from Turkish into English?
Her novels have been translated into forty languages.

senses.def: to result in something, or to change into a different form
examples: Higher sales didn't translate into higher profits.
It's hard to translate these ideas into action.

note: Use "translate from X into Y". A "translator" works with written text; an "interpreter" with speech.

senses.def: the process of changing words into another language, or a text that has been changed this way
examples: I read the novel in English translation.
Some jokes get lost in translation.

note: "Lost in translation" = meaning that disappears when changed into another language or context.

senses.def: the process of passing something, such as a disease or information, from one person or place to another
examples: Wearing masks reduces the transmission of the virus.
Data transmission is faster on the new network.

senses.def: the act of sending out a radio or television signal, or a program that is sent
examples: The live transmission was interrupted by a power cut.

senses.def: the system in a vehicle that sends power from the engine to the wheels
examples: The mechanic said the car needs a new transmission.

senses.def: to send an electronic signal, broadcast, or message
examples: The satellite transmits images back to Earth every hour.
The concert will be transmitted live on the radio.

senses.def: to pass something, such as a disease or knowledge, from one person or thing to another
examples: The disease is transmitted by mosquitoes.
Parents transmit their values to their children.

note: Spelling: transmitted, transmitting (double t).

senses.def: the quality of being open and honest, so that people can see how decisions are made
examples: Voters are demanding more transparency in government spending.
The company promised greater transparency about how it uses customer data.

senses.def: the quality of being clear enough to see through
examples: The transparency of the water lets you see fish twenty feet down.

note: Often paired with "accountability" in political and business language.

senses.def: clear enough that you can see through it
examples: The food is stored in transparent plastic containers.
The insect's wings are almost transparent.

senses.def: open and honest, without secrets
examples: The hiring process should be fair and transparent.

senses.def: (of a lie or excuse) easy to see through or understand
examples: His excuse was a transparent attempt to avoid blame.

note: Opposite: opaque (for materials); secretive (for organizations).

senses.def: to take people or goods from one place to another in a vehicle
examples: The trucks transport fresh produce from farms to supermarkets.
Injured hikers were transported to the hospital by helicopter.

senses.def: a system or method for carrying people or goods from one place to another
examples: The cost of transport makes up a large part of the price.
Air transport is responsible for a growing share of emissions.

note: Verb stress: trans-PORT; noun stress: TRANS-port. For the system, Americans usually say "transportation"; "public transport" is British.

senses.def: a system or vehicles for carrying people or goods, or the act of moving them
examples: Public transportation in New York runs 24 hours a day.
The price includes hotel and transportation to the airport.

note: This is the usual American word; British English prefers "transport".

senses.def: a device for catching animals, or a trick to catch or deceive someone
examples: We set a mouse trap under the sink.
The police set a trap to catch the thief.

senses.def: an unpleasant situation that is hard to escape from
examples: Many families fall into a debt trap.

senses.def: to keep someone in a dangerous place they can't escape from, or to catch someone by a trick
examples: Dozens of miners were trapped underground after the collapse.
She felt trapped in a job she hated.

note: Spelling: trapped, trapping. "Mahsur kalmak" = be trapped / be stranded.

senses.def: a mental condition caused by severe shock, fear, or stress, often with long-lasting effects
examples: Many soldiers suffer from trauma after returning home.
The children needed counseling to deal with the trauma of the earthquake.

senses.def: a serious physical injury
examples: The patient was rushed to the trauma center with head injuries.

senses.def: to go from one place to another, especially over a long distance
examples: She travels to Asia for work several times a year.
We traveled across the country by train.

senses.def: to move or spread from one place to another
examples: Light travels faster than sound.
News travels fast in a small town.

senses.def: the activity of traveling
examples: Air travel has become much cheaper.
Her job involves a lot of travel.

note: American: traveled, traveling; British: travelled, travelling. "Travel" (noun) is uncountable; for one occasion use "a trip".

senses.def: a person who is traveling or who travels often
examples: The airport lounge was packed with tired travellers waiting for delayed flights.
As an experienced traveller, she always packs light.

note: British spelling. American spelling is "traveler" (one l), as in "traveler's checks".

senses.def: a collection of valuable things such as gold, silver, and jewels
examples: The divers found treasure on a ship that sank in 1715.
The kids drew a map to the buried treasure in the backyard.

senses.def: a very valuable object, or a person who is very helpful
examples: The museum is full of national treasures.

senses.def: to value something very much
examples: I'll always treasure the memories of that summer.

senses.def: to behave toward someone or deal with something in a particular way
examples: She treats her employees with respect.
Please treat this information as confidential.

senses.def: to give medical care to a person, illness, or injury
examples: The doctor treated him for a broken arm.
The infection can be treated with antibiotics.

senses.def: to pay for something special for someone or for yourself
examples: Let me treat you to dinner for your birthday.

senses.def: something special and enjoyable that you give someone or do for yourself
examples: Put your wallet away; lunch is my treat.
The kids got ice cream as a treat.

note: "It's my treat" = Ben ısmarlıyorum. "Treat someone to something" = pay for it as a gift.

senses.def: medical care given to cure an illness or injury
examples: She is receiving treatment for cancer.
There is no effective treatment for the disease yet.

senses.def: the way someone behaves toward or deals with a person or thing
examples: The report criticized the treatment of prisoners.
He complained about unfair treatment at work.

note: "Special treatment" = being treated better than others (ayrıcalıklı muamele).

senses.def: a formal written agreement between two or more countries
examples: The two countries signed a peace treaty in 1979.
The treaty bans the testing of nuclear weapons.

note: "Ratify" a treaty = officially approve it. Lausanne Treaty = Lausanne Antlaşması.

senses.def: a tall plant with a wooden trunk, branches, and usually leaves
examples: The kids climbed the old oak tree in the backyard.
Hundreds of trees were knocked down in the storm.

note: "Family tree" = soy ağacı. "Bark up the wrong tree" = look for something in the wrong place.

senses.def: very great in amount, size, or degree
examples: The new job puts tremendous pressure on her.
The volunteers have done a tremendous amount of work.

senses.def: (informal) extremely good
examples: The band gave a tremendous performance last night.

senses.def: a general direction in which a situation is changing or developing
examples: There is a growing trend toward working from home.
The data show a downward trend in crime rates.

senses.def: a new style or fashion that is popular for a time
examples: She always follows the latest fashion trends.

note: "Trending" = currently popular online: "The hashtag is trending."

senses.def: a formal examination of evidence in court to decide if someone is guilty of a crime
examples: The trial is expected to last three weeks.
He is on trial for murder.

senses.def: a test of how well something works or how good it is
examples: The new drug is still in clinical trials.
Sign up for a free 30-day trial.

note: "Trial and error" = learning by trying different ways until one works (deneme yanılma).

senses.def: connected with a tribe or tribes
examples: Tribal leaders met with government officials to discuss land rights.
The museum displays tribal art from across Africa.

senses.def: showing strong loyalty to your own group and distrust of others
examples: American politics has become increasingly tribal.

senses.def: a social group in a traditional society sharing the same language, culture, and often a leader
examples: The tribe has lived in the rainforest for centuries.
Several Native American tribes run casinos on their land.

senses.def: (informal) a group of people with shared interests or identity
examples: Online, she found her tribe of fellow science-fiction fans.

senses.def: a special court with authority to deal with a particular problem or disagreement
examples: An international tribunal was set up to try war crimes.
The employment tribunal ruled that she had been unfairly dismissed.

senses.def: an act, statement, or gift that shows respect or admiration, especially for someone who has died
examples: Fans left flowers outside the stadium as a tribute to the late coach.
The concert was a tribute to the victims of the attack.

senses.def: a sign of how good or effective something is
examples: Her quick recovery is a tribute to the skill of her doctors.

note: "Pay tribute to" = publicly praise or honor (saygılarını sunmak, anmak).

senses.def: something done to deceive someone, or to make them look silly as a joke
examples: The kids played a trick on their teacher on April Fools' Day.
It was all a trick to get my bank details.

senses.def: a clever act done to entertain, or a clever way of doing something
examples: The magician did a card trick.
The trick is to add the salt at the end.

senses.def: to make someone believe something false, especially to cheat them
examples: Scammers tricked her into sending them $5,000.

note: "That should do the trick" = that should solve the problem. "Tricky" = difficult, needing care.

senses.def: to make something happen suddenly
examples: The announcement triggered a wave of protests.
Smoke from the toaster triggered the fire alarm.

senses.def: the part of a gun that you press to fire it
examples: He pulled the trigger, but the gun didn't fire.

senses.def: something that causes a reaction or a series of events
examples: Stress is a common trigger for migraines.

note: "Pull the trigger" can also mean finally make a decision: "We pulled the trigger on the deal."

senses.def: the number 1,000,000,000,000 (one million million)
examples: The US national debt has passed $30 trillion.
The economy is worth about two trillion dollars.

note: No -s after a number: "three trillion dollars". Trillion (10¹²) = Turkish "trilyon"; billion (10⁹) = "milyar".
